summary.name: Highball
summary.one_liner: Highball is a free, open-source, notarized macOS app that runs Windows games on Apple Silicon through Wine, choosing the graphics layer per game from an open compatibility database.
use_cases: Playing Steam games on an Apple Silicon Mac
Running Epic Games library on macOS
Checking whether a Windows game works on Mac before downloading
Browsing an open database of per-game Wine and renderer fixes
Running Windows games without buying a Windows licence or VM
summary.what_it_does: Highball is a macOS app that installs a Wine engine automatically on first run and sets up Windows Steam with one click. It can connect an existing Epic account and launch Epic titles through the open-source Legendary client. Each game gets a verdict (verified, reported, predicted or blocked) and, where a verified fix exists, Highball can apply it. The compatibility data is open and includes provenance and dates for each claim. The page says it tests games by hand on Apple Silicon, and it flags kernel anti-cheat games as impossible before download.
notable: Per-game verdicts and provenance from an open compatibility database, with no account or telemetry
Engine defined in a manifest pinned by hash; community Wine 10 by default, with an own Wine 11 build from CrossOver's published sources
Flags kernel anti-cheat games (e.g. Valorant, Fortnite) as impossible before download, with an explanation
Applies verified per-game fixes, e.g. disabling HDR for Portal 2 to fix freezing
caveats: First run takes about 20 minutes while the engine and Steam download and update
Kernel anti-cheat games cannot run under any compatibility layer, so titles such as Valorant, Fortnite, Destiny 2 and Call of Duty are marked impossible
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon
